source_candidate.source_claim: Final public CLDD detector tuning is explicitly a 10-stream mean-F1 optimization; exact winning detector hyperparameters are outside public Git and not recoverable from the released parquet schema.

findings.claim: The final public source tunes each detector on ten frozen training/error streams and evaluates on a separate ten-seed set.
findings.evidence: At 7b0a474, dodo.py sets N_TRIALS=10, derives ERROR_STREAM_SEEDS from random.Random(0) and EVALUATION_SEEDS from random.Random(1), each with ten draws. task_tune_hp_detector collects one oracle error-stream file for every ERROR_STREAM_SEEDS trial and passes the full list to detector tuning.

findings.claim: Detector tuning uses a 30-trial Optuna search maximizing mean my_f1 over all supplied error streams.
findings.evidence: config/hp/detector.yml sets n_trials=30, metric=my_f1, maximize=true. DDHPSearch evaluates every trial on every supplied frozen stream, averages metrics across streams, stores n_streams, and returns the mean configured metric as the objective.

findings.claim: The historical source used five training streams while retaining ten held-out evaluation streams, and a later source switched training/error streams to ten.
findings.evidence: At a78a871c... ERROR_STREAM_SEEDS uses range(5) while EVALUATION_SEEDS uses N_TRIALS=10. At f186455e... both use N_TRIALS=10.
findings.scope: This verifies the source-code protocol change. It does not by itself identify which exact ignored tuned-parameter artifact generated every externally released numerical table/dataset.

findings.claim: The exact winning detector hyperparameters and full best-trial record are produced by the public code but retained in public Git history.
findings.evidence: main.py trial_to_yml writes best_params.yml and best_trial.yml under the tuning log directory, while .gitignore excludes the entire logs directory. Repository code search at the pinned public head finds references to best_params.yml but no tracked result file containing the winning values.
findings.scope: An external archive, release attachment, execution receipt, or untracked log copy could still contain the values; this audit establishes absence from the inspected public Git tree, not universal nonexistence.

findings.claim: The released CLDD parquet schema is sufficient to recover the winning detector hyperparameters or Optuna trial provenance.
findings.evidence: collect_dataset serializes boundary, strategy, detector, seed, error_stream, trues, preds, max_delay, and max_early. It does not serialize detector config/parameters, trial number, best objective value, source SHA, dependency version, or best-trial metadata.
findings.scope: The parquet remains useful for row/seed/event-array and detector-metric recomputation; it cannot alone bind those rows to the exact winning hyperparameter artifact.

material_interpretation: The worker's revised CLDD provenance claim is supported. Current public code defines a 10-training-stream, 10-held-out-stream, 30-trial mean-my_f1 detector-tuning contract, while older source used five training streams. Exact winning detector parameters remain a separate provenance object that is generated under ignored logs and omitted from the parquet schema; therefore final numerical reproduction requires recovering a source-matched best_params/best_trial artifact or rerunning the search under a pinned environment.

downstream_use.correction: Version CLDD claims explicitly: five-stream historical source versus ten-stream final public source. Do not infer exact uploaded-dataset detector HP from the parquet alone.
do_not_generalize: Do not call the public source irreproducible merely because winning HP files are not committed; the search algorithm is public and can be rerun under a pinned environment.
Do not claim the released parquet proves whether five-stream or ten-stream winning parameters generated a particular upload without an external binding artifact.
Do not merge training/error seeds and held-out evaluation seeds; they are generated from distinct RNG instances.
